{"body":"## Summary

- OpenCode (≥v1.3.x) stopped reliably emitting `session.status` events with `status.type === "idle"` and now emits `session.idle` events instead
- The plugin only listened for `session.status`, so `turn-end` hooks stopped firing entirely after ~March 19
- Added `session.idle` as a fall-through case alongside `session.status` for cross-version compatibility

## Problem

The Entire OpenCode plugin detects when the agent finishes a turn by listening for `session.status` events where `status.type === "idle"`. After a recent OpenCode update, these events stopped being emitted — OpenCode now sends `session.idle` events instead.

**Impact chain:**
1. `turn-end` hook never fires → `PrepareTranscript` never runs
2. `opencode export <sessionID>` never called → transcript file (`.entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json`) never created
3. Post-commit condensation fails silently: `"transcript not found at .entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json: file does not exist"`
4. `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is still added to commits, but no session data is written to `entire/checkpoints/v1`
5. Checkpoint directories on GitHub are empty (e.g., `entire/checkpoints/v1/67/f7ac0243e0/`)

**Evidence from logs** — many turn-starts, zero turn-ends, repeated condensation failures:
```
12:25:35 prepare-commit-msg: agent commit trailer added checkpoint_id: "67f7ac0243e0"
12:25:37 condensation failed: transcript not found at .entire/tmp/ses_2e0e2d753ffeK502gNjKLGmkbu.json: file does not exist
```

## Fix

Handle both event types as a fall-through case in the switch statement. `session.idle` has `properties.sessionID` directly, while `session.status` has `properties.status.type` that must be checked for `"idle"`. The fix branches on `event.type` to extract the session ID correctly from each shape.

## Test plan

- [ ] Start an OpenCode session with `entire enable --agent opencode` applied
- [ ] Make changes and commit — verify `turn-end` appears in `.entire/logs/entire.log`
- [ ] Verify transcript file is created at `.entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json`
- [ ] Verify `session condensed` log entry with non-zero `transcript_lines`
- [ ] Push and verify checkpoint data appears on `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on GitHub

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Moderate risk because it changes session lifecycle/turn-end detection and could affect when `turn-end` fires (missed or duplicated) across different OpenCode event shapes, though the change is small and localized.
> 
> **Overview**
> Improves cross-version compatibility for turn completion detection by handling `session.idle` in addition to `session.status` with `status.type === "idle"`, extracting `sessionID` appropriately for each event shape.
> 
> This ensures the synchronous `turn-end` hook is still invoked when OpenCode versions stop emitting the idle `session.status` event.
> 
> <sup>Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit fdf6278bb24ad3912dc3cfb24840a3dce4dfcd6f. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->","title":"fix(opencode): handle session.idle event for turn-end detection","url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/771"}

index 8544aa59a..d0bbefa70 100644
--- a/cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin.ts
+++ b/cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin.ts
@@ -115,12 +115,19 @@ export const EntirePlugin: Plugin = async ({ directory }) => {
             break
           }
 
+          case "session.idle":
           case "session.status": {
-            // session.status fires in both TUI and non-interactive (run) mode.
-            // session.idle is deprecated and not reliably emitted in run mode.
-            const props = (event as any).properties
-            if (props?.status?.type !== "idle") break
-            const sessionID = props?.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
+            // session.status fires with status.type "idle" when the agent finishes.
+            // session.idle is a separate event that some OpenCode versions emit instead.
+            // Handle both for compatibility across OpenCode versions.
+            let sessionID: string | null = null
+            if (event.type === "session.idle") {
+              sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
+            } else {
+              const props = (event as any).properties
+              if (props?.status?.type !== "idle") break
+              sessionID = props?.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
+            }
             if (!sessionID) break
             // Use sync variant: `opencode run` exits on the same idle event,
             // so an async hook would be killed before completing.

    88→## Event System
    89→
    90→### Single Event Handler Pattern
    91→
    92→Our plugin uses a **single `event` handler** with type-based dispatching:
    93→
    94→```typescript
    95→export default {
    96→  name: "entire-integration",
    97→  version: "0.1.0",
    98→  hooks: {
    99→    event: async (input) => {
   100→      switch (input.type) {
   101→        case "session.created":
   102→          await handleSessionCreated(input)
   103→          break
   104→        case "session.idle":
   105→          await handleSessionIdle(input)
   106→          break
   107→        case "session.stopped":
   108→          await handleSessionStopped(input)
   109→          break
   110→      }
   111→    }
   112→  }
   113→}
   114→```
   115→
   116→**Why single handler?**
   117→- Simplifies lifecycle management
   118→- All session events in one place
   119→- Matches patterns in `opencode-helicone-session`, `opencode-supermemory`
   120→- Easy to add new event types without changing plugin structure
   121→
   122→### Event Types We Handle
   123→
   124→1. **`session.created`** - Session starts
   125→   - Initialize session tracking
   126→   - Create export directory
   127→   - Log session start
   128→
   129→2. **`session.idle`** - Session becomes idle (10+ minutes no activity)
   130→   - Export transcript snapshot
   131→   - Parse transcript for metadata (Phase 2A)
   132→   - Call Entire CLI stop hook with task/todo metadata
   133→
   134→3. **`session.stopped`** - Session ends (unused, but available)
   135→   - Export final transcript
   136→   - Call Entire CLI hook
   137→   - Process metadata and commit
   138→
   139→4. **`message.part.updated`** - Tool state changes (Phase 2B)
   140→   - Track Task tool lifecycle (pending → running → completed/error)
   141→   - Call pre-task hook (task-start) when Task starts
   142→   - Call post-task hook (task-complete) when Task finishes
   143→   - Export and link subagent transcripts
   144→

   149→hooks: {
   150→  event: async (input) => { /* existing handler */ },
   151→  'chat.message': async (input, output) => {
   152→    // Incremental export during long sessions

   158→## Critical: Non-Blocking Patterns
   159→
   160→### ⚠️ NEVER Block OpenCode Startup
   161→
   162→OpenCode plugins run during CLI initialization. Any blocking operation will freeze the entire OpenCode CLI.
   163→
   164→#### ❌ **WRONG - Blocks OpenCode**
   165→```typescript
   166→// BAD: Bun's shell API blocks
   167→const result = await this.$`which entire`
   168→
   169→// BAD: Awaiting logger calls blocks
   170→await this.client.app.log({ level, message })
   171→
   172→// BAD: Long synchronous operations
   173→const result = execSync("some-slow-command")
   174→```
   175→
   176→#### ✅ **CORRECT - Non-Blocking**
   177→```typescript
   178→// GOOD: Node's execSync with timeout
   179→import { execSync } from "child_process"
   180→try {
   181→  execSync("which entire", { stdio: "ignore", timeout: 2000 })
   182→} catch (e) {
   183→  return false
   184→}
   185→
   186→// GOOD: Fire-and-forget logging with timeout
   187→const logPromise = this.client.app.log({ level, message })
   188→Promise.race([
   189→  logPromise,
   190→  new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000))
   191→]).catch(() => {}) // Ignore failures
   192→
   193→// GOOD: Async operations for hooks (not startup)
   194→await entireCLI.callHook("stop", hookInput) // OK during session hooks
   195→```
   196→
   197→### Historical Issues We Fixed
   198→
   199→**Issue 1: Plugin Hung on Startup**
   200→- **Symptom:** OpenCode froze after loading plugin, no output
   201→- **Cause:** Used Bun's `this.$\`which entire\`` which blocks
   202→- **Fix:** Replaced with Node's `execSync` + timeout
   203→- **File:** `src/cli/entire.ts:isInstalled()`
   204→
   205→**Issue 2: Logger Blocking**
   206→- **Symptom:** Random hangs during initialization
   207→- **Cause:** Awaiting `client.app.log()` blocked execution
   208→- **Fix:** Fire-and-forget with Promise.race() timeout
   209→- **File:** `src/utils/logger.ts`

   211→## CLI Integration
   212→
   213→### Stdin Piping Pattern
   214→
   215→#### ❌ **WRONG - Bun Shell Doesn't Pass Stdin**
   216→```typescript
   217→await this.$`entire hooks opencode stop`.stdin(JSON.stringify(input))
   218→```
   219→
   220→#### ✅ **CORRECT - Node's spawnSync With Input**
   221→```typescript
   222→import { spawnSync } from "child_process"
   223→const result = spawnSync("entire", ["hooks", "opencode", hookName], {
   224→  input: JSON.stringify(input),  // Passed via stdin
   225→  encoding: "utf-8",
   226→  timeout: 10000,
   227→})
   228→```
   229→
   230→**Why:** Bun's shell API doesn't properly pipe stdin to child processes. Node's `child_process` does.
   231→
   232→**Note:** This JSON stdin pattern is unique to this plugin. Most OpenCode plugins call simpler CLIs using just arguments or environment variables. Our pattern is intentional for Entire CLI's structured hook architecture.
   233→
   234→### Hook Input Format
   235→
   236→All hooks receive JSON via stdin:
   237→```typescript
   238→interface EntireHookInput {
   239→  session_id: string        // OpenCode session ID (e.g., "ses_abc123")
   240→  session_ref: string       // Same as session_id for OpenCode
   241→  timestamp: string         // ISO 8601 format
   242→  transcript_path: string   // Path to exported transcript
   243→}
   244→```
   245→
   246→**Contract:** The plugin is responsible for constructing this input correctly. The CLI handles agent detection and metadata processing internally.

   281→## Pattern Decisions
   282→
   283→This section documents architectural choices that differ from typical OpenCode plugins. These are **intentional design decisions**, not bugs or oversights.
   284→
   285→### Single Event Handler vs Multiple Hooks
   286→
   287→**Our Choice:** Single `event` handler with type-based dispatching
   288→
   289→**Rationale:**
   290→- Session lifecycle events (created, idle, stopped) are all we need for Phase 1
   291→- Keeps implementation simple and focused
   292→- Matches pattern used by `opencode-helicone-session` and `opencode-supermemory`
   293→
   294→**Future Consideration:** Phase 2 could add `chat.message` hook for incremental transcript exports during long sessions (pattern used by `opencode-wakatime`). This would reduce data loss if sessions crash.
   295→
   296→### JSON via Stdin vs CLI Arguments
   297→
   298→**Our Choice:** Pass structured JSON to Entire CLI via stdin
   299→
   300→**Rationale:**
   301→- Hook input is complex (session_id, timestamp, transcript_path, metadata)
   302→- JSON ensures proper escaping and type safety
   303→- Entire CLI's hook architecture expects structured input
   304→- Most other plugins have simpler CLI interactions (e.g., `git rev-parse`, `wakatime --heartbeat`)
   305→
   306→**Alternative Considered:** CLI arguments like `entire hooks opencode stop --session-id=... --timestamp=...`
   307→- Rejected: Harder to maintain, escaping issues, limited extensibility
   308→
   309→### Project-Scoped Export Location
   310→
   311→**Our Choice:** Export to `.entire/tmp/opencode/` (project-local)
   312→
   313→**Rationale:**
   314→- Session data is tied to specific git repositories
   315→- Multiple projects can have separate session histories
   316→- Aligns with `.entire/` directory convention used by Entire CLI
   317→- Clear separation: OpenCode's data vs Entire's processed metadata
   318→
   319→**Alternative Considered:** Global location like `~/.config/opencode/entire/`
   320→- Rejected: Sessions lose project context, harder to associate with repos
   321→
   322→### No Custom Tools (Phase 1)
   323→
   324→**Our Choice:** Event handlers only, no custom tools exposed to Claude
   325→
   326→**Rationale:**
   327→- Phase 1 focuses on session tracking and metadata extraction
   328→- Event-driven architecture is sufficient for automatic tracking
   329→- Keeps initial implementation simple
   330→
   331→**Future Consideration:** Phase 2 could add custom tools:
   332→- `entire_checkpoint` - Create manual checkpoint with description
   333→- `entire_rewind` - View available rewind points
   334→- `entire_stats` - Show session statistics
   335→- Pattern used by `opencode-scheduler` (6 tools) and `opencode-skillful` (3 tools)

   371→## Common Pitfalls
   372→
   373→### 1. Blocking Operations in Plugin Initialization
   374→**Symptom:** OpenCode hangs on startup
   375→**Solution:** Use timeouts, fire-and-forget patterns, or defer to hooks
   376→
   377→### 2. Stdin Not Reaching CLI
   378→**Symptom:** CLI reports "failed to parse hook input"
   379→**Solution:** Use Node's `spawnSync` with `input` parameter, not Bun shell
   380→
   381→### 3. Missing Hook Input Fields
   382→**Symptom:** CLI hook execution fails with "missing required field"
   383→**Solution:** Ensure all required fields in `EntireHookInput` are provided:
   384→- `session_id` - OpenCode session ID
   385→- `session_ref` - Same as session_id
   386→- `timestamp` - ISO 8601 format
   387→- `transcript_path` - Absolute path to exported transcript
   388→
   389→### 4. Path Confusion
   390→**Symptom:** Transcript file not found
   391→**Solution:**
   392→- Always export to `.entire/tmp/opencode/sessions/<session-id>/`
   393→- Pass absolute path to CLI in `transcript_path`
   394→- Never use relative paths in hook input

    52→
    53→    // Parse transcript
    54→    const parsed = parseTranscript(messages)
    55→
    56→    logger.debug("Parsed transcript metadata", {
    57→      sessionID,
    58→      taskSpawns: parsed.taskSpawns.length,
    59→      todos: parsed.todos.length,
    60→      toolCalls: parsed.toolCalls.length,
    61→    })
    62→
    63→    // Build metadata object based on config
    64→    const metadata: Partial<EntireHookInput> = {}
    65→
    66→    if (config.enable_task_tracking) {
    67→      metadata.task_spawns = parsed.taskSpawns
    68→      metadata.tool_stats = parsed.toolStats
    69→    }
    70→
    71→    if (config.enable_todo_tracking) {
    72→      metadata.todos = parsed.todos
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    return metadata
    76→  } catch (error) {
    77→    logger.warn("Failed to parse session metadata", {
    78→      sessionID,
    79→      error: String(error),
    80→    })
    81→    return {}
    82→  }
    83→}
    84→
    85→export function createSessionHooks(
    86→  ctx: PluginInput,
    87→  config: EntireConfig,
    88→  entireCLI: EntireCLI,
    89→  logger: Logger
    90→) {
    91→  const { client, directory } = ctx
    92→
    93→  return {
    94→    /**
    95→     * Handle session.created event
    96→     * Initializes session tracking in Entire CLI
    97→     */
    98→    async onSessionCreated({ event }: SessionEvent): Promise<void> {
    99→      const sessionID = event.properties.info?.id
   100→      if (!sessionID) {
   101→        logger.warn("session.created event missing session ID")
   102→        return
   103→      }
   104→
   105→      try {
   106→        logger.debug("Session created", { sessionID })
   107→
   108→        // Export transcript and metadata
   109→        let transcriptPath = ""
   110→        if (config.export_transcripts) {
   111→          const exported = await exportTranscript(sessionID, client, directory)
   112→          transcriptPath = exported.path
   113→          logger.debug("Exported transcript", {
   114→            sessionID,
   115→            path: transcriptPath,
   116→            messageCount: exported.messageCount,
   117→          })
   118→
   119→          // Export session metadata
   120→          await exportMetadata(sessionID, event.properties.info, directory)
   121→        }
   122→
   123→        // Call entire hooks opencode session-start
   124→        await entireCLI.callHook("session-start", {
   125→          session_id: sessionID,
   126→          session_ref: sessionID,
   127→          timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
   128→          transcript_path: transcriptPath,
   129→        })
   130→
   131→        logger.info("Session tracking initialized", { sessionID })
   132→      } catch (error) {
   133→        logger.error("Failed to initialize session tracking", {
   134→          sessionID,
   135→          error: String(error),
   136→        })
   137→      }
   138→    },
   139→
   140→    /**
   141→     * Handle session.idle event
   142→     * Saves checkpoint when session goes idle
   143→     */
   144→    async onSessionIdle({ event }: SessionEvent): Promise<void> {
   145→      const sessionID = event.properties.sessionID
   146→      if (!sessionID) {
   147→        logger.warn("session.idle event missing session ID")
   148→        return
   149→      }
   150→
   151→      try {
   152→        logger.debug("Session idle", { sessionID })
   153→
   154→        // Export transcript
   155→        let transcriptPath = ""
   156→        if (config.export_transcripts) {
   157→          const exported = await exportTranscript(sessionID, client, directory)
   158→          transcriptPath = exported.path
   159→          logger.debug("Exported transcript on idle", {
   160→            sessionID,
   161→            path: transcriptPath,
   162→            messageCount: exported.messageCount,
   163→          })
   164→        }
   165→
   166→        // Parse session metadata (Phase 2A: task spawns, todos, tool stats)
   167→        const metadata = await parseSessionMetadata(sessionID, client, config, logger)
   168→
   169→        // Build hook input with all metadata
   170→        const hookInput: EntireHookInput = {
   171→          session_id: sessionID,
   172→          session_ref: sessionID,
   173→          timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
   174→          transcript_path: transcriptPath,
   175→          ...metadata,
   176→        }
   177→
   178→        // Call entire hooks opencode stop
   179→        await entireCLI.callHook("stop", hookInput)
   180→
   181→        logger.info("Session checkpoint saved", {
   182→          sessionID,
   183→          taskSpawns: metadata.task_spawns?.length || 0,
   184→          todos: metadata.todos?.length || 0,
   185→        })
   186→      } catch (error) {
   187→        logger.warn("Failed to save session checkpoint", {
   188→          sessionID,
   189→          error: String(error),
   190→        })
   191→      }
   192→    },
   193→
   194→    /**
   195→     * Handle session.status event
   196→     * Could be used for periodic checkpoints (currently just logs)
   197→     */
   198→    onSessionStatus({ event }: SessionEvent): void {
   199→      const sessionID = event.properties.sessionID
   200→      if (!sessionID) {
   201→        return
   202→      }
   203→
   204→      logger.debug("Session status update", { sessionID })
   205→      // Future: could implement periodic checkpointing here
   206→    },
   207→  }
   208→}

1→# OpenCode Entire Integration
     2→
     3→Track your OpenCode sessions with git-based version control using Entire CLI.
     4→
     5→## What is this?
     6→
     7→This plugin connects [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) (multi-agent AI CLI) with [Entire CLI](https://entire.io/cli) (git session manager) to:
     8→
     9→- 📝 Track all your OpenCode sessions as git checkpoints
    10→- ⏮️ Rewind to any point in your AI-assisted development
    11→- 🔗 **Track subagent spawns** - See which Task agents were spawned during your session
    12→- ✅ **Extract todo lists** - Automatically capture your task progress
    13→- 📊 Export session transcripts and tool usage statistics for review
    14→
    15→## Status
    16→

    18→
    19→- ✅ Session lifecycle tracking (created, idle)

    26→- ✅ Integration with Entire CLI git strategies (manual-commit, auto-commit)

    78→## Features
    79→
    80→### Automatic Session Tracking
    81→Every OpenCode session is automatically tracked with:
    82→- **Session titles** - OpenCode's AI-generated summary of your request
    83→- **User prompts** - All prompts you entered during the session
    84→- **File changes** - Automatic detection of modified, new, and deleted files
    85→- **Context summaries** - Rich markdown summaries of the conversation
    86→
    87→### Task & Todo Tracking (Phase 2)
    88→Track your AI workflow with automatic extraction of:
    89→- **Subagent spawns** - See which Task agents were spawned (Explore, Plan, etc.)
    90→- **Todo lists** - Automatically capture your task progress and status changes
    91→- **Tool usage statistics** - Track all tool calls with success/error counts
    92→
    93→### Task Lifecycle Hooks (Phase 2B)
    94→Real-time tracking of subagent work with:
    95→- **Pre-task hooks** - Triggered when Task tools start (pending/running states)
    96→- **Post-task hooks** - Triggered when Task tools complete, with automatic subagent transcript export
    97→- **Subagent transcript linking** - Child session transcripts automatically exported and linked to parent
    98→- **Task hierarchy tracking** - Active task states tracked in memory for monitoring
    99→
   100→### Git Integration
   101→- **Commit trailers** - Your commits are automatically linked to OpenCode sessions
   102→- **Shadow branches** - Session metadata stored in git without cluttering your history
   103→- **Rewind support** - Roll back to any point in your AI-assisted development
   104→- **Multiple strategies** - Choose between manual-commit (clean history) or auto-commit

   148→## Configuration
   149→
   150→Create `.entire/opencode/config.json` in your repository to customize behavior:
   151→
   152→```json
   153→{
   154→  "enable_task_tracking": true,
   155→  "enable_todo_tracking": true,
   156→  "export_transcripts": true,
   157→  "hook_timeout_ms": 5000,
   158→  "log_level": "info",
   159→  "debounce_ms": 500
   160→}
   161→```
   162→
   163→### Configuration Options
   164→
   165→| Option | Type | Default | Description |
   166→|--------|------|---------|-------------|
   167→| `export_transcripts` | boolean | `true` | **✅ Active** - Export session transcripts to files |
   168→| `hook_timeout_ms` | number | `5000` | **✅ Active** - Hook execution timeout in milliseconds |
   169→| `log_level` | string | `"info"` | **✅ Active** - Log level: debug, info, warn, error |
   170→| `enable_task_tracking` | boolean | `true` | **✅ Active (Phase 2A)** - Track subagent spawns and tool stats |
   171→| `enable_todo_tracking` | boolean | `true` | **✅ Active (Phase 2A)** - Extract todo metadata from sessions |
   172→| `debounce_ms` | number | `500` | **⏳ Future** - Debounce rapid events |
   173→
   174→## How It Works
   175→
   176→```
   177→OpenCode CLI → Plugin (TypeScript) → Entire CLI (Go) → Git Operations
   178→     ↓              ↓                        ↓                  ↓
   179→  Events     Translate Events      Strategy Pattern      Shadow Branches
   180→             Export Transcripts    Handle Git Ops        Metadata Storage
   181→```
   182→
   183→1. **OpenCode** publishes events when sessions start, end, tools execute, etc.
   184→2. **Plugin** subscribes to these events and exports session data
   185→3. **Entire CLI** receives hook calls and performs git operations
   186→4. **Git** stores session history in shadow branches with metadata

   189→
   190→```
   191→your-project/
   192→├── .entire/
   193→│   ├── settings.json           # Entire CLI configuration

   199→│   │           └── <session-id>/

   201→│   │               └── metadata.json
   202→│   └── metadata/               # Processed session metadata (gitignored)
   203→│       └── <entire-session-id>/

   206→│           └── context.md      # Generated context summary
   207→├── .git/
   208→│   ├── entire-sessions/        # Session state files (shared across worktrees)
   209→│   └── refs/heads/

   343→## Architecture
   344→
   345→### Plugin Structure
   346→
   347→```
   348→src/
   349→├── index.ts                    # Main plugin entry
   350→├── types.ts                    # TypeScript definitions
   351→├── hooks/
   352→│   ├── session.ts              # Session lifecycle hooks
   353→│   └── task.ts                 # Task lifecycle hooks (Phase 2B)
   354→├── export/
   355→│   ├── transcript.ts           # Transcript export
   356→│   └── parser.ts               # Transcript parser (Phase 2A)
   357→├── cli/
   358→│   └── entire.ts               # Entire CLI wrapper
   359→└── utils/
   360→    ├── logger.ts               # Logging utilities
   361→    └── config.ts               # Configuration management
   362→```
   363→
   364→### Event Flow
   365→
   366→**On Session Start:**
   367→1. **OpenCode event** → `session.created`
   368→2. **Plugin hook** → `onSessionCreated()`
   369→3. **Export transcript** → `.entire/tmp/opencode/sessions/<id>/transcript.jsonl`
   370→4. **Call Entire CLI** → `entire hooks opencode session-start`
   371→
   372→**On Session Idle (checkpoint creation):**
   373→1. **OpenCode event** → `session.idle` (after ~30s of inactivity)
   374→2. **Plugin hook** → `onSessionIdle()`
   375→3. **Export updated transcript** → `.entire/tmp/opencode/sessions/<id>/transcript.jsonl`
   376→4. **Call Entire CLI** → `entire hooks opencode stop`
   377→5. **CLI processes transcript:**
   378→   - Parse OpenCode JSONL format
   379→   - Extract user prompts and session title
   380→   - Detect modified/new/deleted files
   381→   - Generate context summary
   382→6. **CLI creates metadata** → `.entire/metadata/<entire-session-id>/`
   383→   - `full.jsonl` - Copied transcript
   384→   - `prompt.txt` - User prompts (title as first line)
   385→   - `context.md` - Session context summary
   386→7. **Git operations:**
   387→   - Create checkpoint on shadow branch (`entire/<commit-hash>`)
   388→   - Store metadata in git tree
   389→8. **Result** → Session tracked with full metadata
   390→
   391→**On User Commit:**
   392→1. **Git hook** → `prepare-commit-msg`
   393→2. **CLI finds active sessions** with checkpoints
   394→3. **Add trailer** → `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` to commit message
   395→4. **Result** → Commit linked to session metadata
   396→
   397→**On Task Start (Phase 2B):**
   398→1. **OpenCode event** → `message.part.updated` (Task tool state: pending/running)
   399→2. **Plugin hook** → `onMessagePartUpdated()`
   400→3. **Call Entire CLI** → `entire hooks opencode task-start`
   401→4. **Result** → Pre-task checkpoint created
   402→
   403→**On Task Complete (Phase 2B):**
   404→1. **OpenCode event** → `message.part.updated` (Task tool state: completed)
   405→2. **Plugin hook** → `onMessagePartUpdated()`
   406→3. **Find subagent session** → Query OpenCode for child sessions (by parentID)
   407→4. **Export subagent transcript** → `.entire/tmp/opencode/sessions/<subagent-id>/transcript.jsonl`
   408→5. **Call Entire CLI** → `entire hooks opencode task-complete` (with subagent_transcript_path)
   409→6. **Result** → Post-task checkpoint with linked subagent transcript

    18→// Hook name constants — these become CLI subcommands under `entire hooks opencode`.
    19→const (
    20→	HookNameSessionStart = "session-start"
    21→	HookNameSessionEnd   = "session-end"
    22→	HookNameTurnStart    = "turn-start"
    23→	HookNameTurnEnd      = "turn-end"
    24→	HookNameCompaction   = "compaction"

    26→
    27→// HookNames returns the hook verbs this agent supports.
    28→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) HookNames() []string {
    29→	return []string{
    30→		HookNameSessionStart,
    31→		HookNameSessionEnd,
    32→		HookNameTurnStart,
    33→		HookNameTurnEnd,
    34→		HookNameCompaction,
    35→	}

    38→// ParseHookEvent translates OpenCode hook calls into normalized lifecycle events.
    39→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ParseHookEvent(ctx context.Context, hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*agent.Event, error) {
    40→	switch hookName {
    41→	case HookNameSessionStart:
    42→		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
    43→		if err != nil {
    44→			return nil, err
    45→		}
    46→		return &agent.Event{
    47→			Type:      agent.SessionStart,
    48→			SessionID: raw.SessionID,
    49→			Timestamp: time.Now(),
    50→		}, nil
    51→
    52→	case HookNameTurnStart:
    53→		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[turnStartRaw](stdin)
    54→		if err != nil {
    55→			return nil, err
    56→		}
    57→		transcriptPath, err := sessionTranscriptPath(ctx, raw.SessionID)
    58→		if err != nil {
    59→			return nil, err
    60→		}
    61→		return &agent.Event{
    62→			Type:       agent.TurnStart,
    63→			SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
    64→			SessionRef: transcriptPath,
    65→			Prompt:     raw.Prompt,
    66→			Model:      raw.Model,
    67→			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
    68→		}, nil
    69→
    70→	case HookNameTurnEnd:
    71→		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[turnEndRaw](stdin)
    72→		if err != nil {
    73→			return nil, err
    74→		}
    75→		// Export is deferred to PrepareTranscript; we just compute the path here.
    76→		transcriptPath, err := sessionTranscriptPath(ctx, raw.SessionID)
    77→		if err != nil {
    78→			return nil, err
    79→		}
    80→		return &agent.Event{
    81→			Type:       agent.TurnEnd,
    82→			SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
    83→			SessionRef: transcriptPath,
    84→			Model:      raw.Model,
    85→			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
    86→		}, nil
    87→
    88→	case HookNameCompaction:
    89→		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
    90→		if err != nil {
    91→			return nil, err
    92→		}
    93→		return &agent.Event{
    94→			Type:      agent.Compaction,
    95→			SessionID: raw.SessionID,
    96→			Timestamp: time.Now(),
    97→		}, nil
    98→
    99→	case HookNameSessionEnd:
   100→		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
   101→		if err != nil {
   102→			return nil, err
   103→		}
   104→		return &agent.Event{
   105→			Type:      agent.SessionEnd,
   106→			SessionID: raw.SessionID,
   107→			Timestamp: time.Now(),
   108→		}, nil
   109→
   110→	default:
   111→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil event = no lifecycle action for unknown hooks
   112→	}
   113→}

   115→// PrepareTranscript ensures the OpenCode transcript file is up-to-date by calling `opencode export`.
   116→// OpenCode's transcript is created/updated via `opencode export`, but condensation may need fresh
   117→// data mid-turn (e.g., during mid-turn commits or resumed sessions where the cached file is stale).
   118→// This method always refreshes the transcript to ensure the latest agent activity is captured.
   119→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) PrepareTranscript(ctx context.Context, sessionRef string) error {
   120→	// Validate the session ref path
   121→	if _, err := os.Stat(sessionRef); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   122→		// Permission denied, broken symlink, or other non-recoverable errors
   123→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to stat OpenCode transcript path %s: %w", sessionRef, err)
   124→	}
   125→
   126→	// Extract session ID from path: basename without .json extension
   127→	base := filepath.Base(sessionRef)
   128→	if !strings.HasSuffix(base, ".json") {
   129→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid OpenCode transcript path (expected .json): %s", sessionRef)
   130→	}
   131→	sessionID := strings.TrimSuffix(base, ".json")
   132→	if sessionID == "" {
   133→		return fmt.Errorf("empty session ID in transcript path: %s", sessionRef)
   134→	}
   135→
   136→	// Always call fetchAndCacheExport to get fresh transcript data.
   137→	// This is critical for resumed sessions where the cached file may contain stale data
   138→	// from a previous turn. Unlike turn-end (which always runs export), mid-turn commits
   139→	// need to refresh the transcript to capture agent activity since the last export.
   140→	_, err := a.fetchAndCacheExport(ctx, sessionID)
   141→	return err
   142→}
   143→
   144→// sessionTranscriptPath validates the session ID and returns the expected transcript path.
   145→func sessionTranscriptPath(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (string, error) {
   146→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   147→		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID for transcript path: %w", err)
   148→	}
   149→	repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
   150→	if err != nil {
   151→		repoRoot = "."
   152→	}
   153→	return filepath.Join(repoRoot, paths.EntireTmpDir, sessionID+".json"), nil
   154→}
   155→
   156→// fetchAndCacheExport calls `opencode export <sessionID>` and writes the result
   157→// to a temporary file. Returns the path to the temp file.
   158→//
   159→// Integration testing: Set ENTIRE_TEST_OPENCODE_MOCK_EXPORT=1 to skip the
   160→// `opencode export` call and use pre-written mock data instead. Tests must
   161→// pre-write the transcript file to .entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json before
   162→// triggering the hook. See integration_test/hooks.go:SimulateOpenCodeTurnEnd.
   163→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) fetchAndCacheExport(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (string, error) {
   164→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   165→		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID for export: %w", err)
   166→	}
   167→
   168→	// Get worktree root for the temp directory
   169→	repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
   170→	if err != nil {
   171→		repoRoot = "."
   172→	}
   173→
   174→	tmpDir := filepath.Join(repoRoot, paths.EntireTmpDir)
   175→	tmpFile := filepath.Join(tmpDir, sessionID+".json")
   176→
   177→	// Integration test mode: use pre-written mock file without calling opencode export
   178→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_OPENCODE_MOCK_EXPORT") != "" {
   179→		if _, err := os.Stat(tmpFile); err == nil {
   180→			return tmpFile, nil
   181→		}
   182→		return "", fmt.Errorf("mock export file not found: %s (ENTIRE_TEST_OPENCODE_MOCK_EXPORT is set)", tmpFile)
   183→	}
   184→
   185→	// Call opencode export to get the transcript (always refresh on each turn)
   186→	data, err := runOpenCodeExport(ctx, sessionID)
   187→	if err != nil {
   188→		return "", fmt.Errorf("opencode export failed: %w", err)
   189→	}
   190→
   191→	// Validate output is valid JSON before caching
   192→	if !json.Valid(data) {
   193→		return "", fmt.Errorf("opencode export returned invalid JSON (%d bytes)", len(data))
   194→	}
   195→
   196→	// Write to temp directory under .entire
   197→	if err := os.MkdirAll(tmpDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   198→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create temp dir: %w", err)
   199→	}
   200→
   201→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   202→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to write export file: %w", err)
   203→	}
   204→
   205→	return tmpFile, nil
   206→}

1→// Entire CLI plugin for OpenCode
     2→// Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode`
     3→// Do not edit manually — changes will be overwritten on next install.
     4→// Requires Bun runtime (used by OpenCode's plugin system for loading ESM plugins).
     5→import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
     6→
     7→export const EntirePlugin: Plugin = async ({ directory }) => {
     8→  const ENTIRE_CMD = '__ENTIRE_CMD__'
     9→  // Track seen user messages to fire turn-start only once per message
    10→  const seenUserMessages = new Set<string>()
    11→  // Track current session ID for message events (which don't include sessionID)
    12→  let currentSessionID: string | null = null
    13→  // Track the model used by the most recent assistant message
    14→  let currentModel: string | null = null
    15→  // In-memory store for message metadata (role, tokens, etc.)
    16→  const messageStore = new Map<string, any>()
    17→
    18→  /**
    19→   * Build the shell command for a hook invocation.
    20→   * Uses sh -c so that shell command substitution in ENTIRE_CMD
    21→   * (e.g., $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) for local-dev) is interpreted.
    22→   */
    23→  function hookCmd(hookName: string): string[] {
    24→    return ["sh", "-c", `${ENTIRE_CMD} hooks opencode ${hookName}`]
    25→  }
    26→
    27→  /**
    28→   * Pipe JSON payload to an entire hooks command (async).
    29→   * Errors are logged but never thrown — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode.
    30→   */
    31→  async function callHook(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
    32→    try {
    33→      const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
    34→      const proc = Bun.spawn(hookCmd(hookName), {
    35→        cwd: directory,
    36→        stdin: new Blob([json + "\n"]),
    37→        stdout: "ignore",
    38→        stderr: "ignore",
    39→      })
    40→      await proc.exited
    41→    } catch {
    42→      // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
    43→    }
    44→  }
    45→
    46→  /**
    47→   * Synchronous variant for hooks that fire near process exit (turn-end, session-end).
    48→   * `opencode run` breaks its event loop on the same session.status idle event that
    49→   * triggers turn-end. The async callHook would be killed before completing.
    50→   * Bun.spawnSync blocks the event loop, preventing exit until the hook finishes.
    51→   */
    52→  function callHookSync(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
    53→    try {
    54→      const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
    55→      Bun.spawnSync(hookCmd(hookName), {
    56→        cwd: directory,
    57→        stdin: new TextEncoder().encode(json + "\n"),
    58→        stdout: "ignore",
    59→        stderr: "ignore",
    60→      })
    61→    } catch {
    62→      // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
    63→    }
    64→  }
    65→
    66→  return {
    67→    event: async ({ event }) => {
    68→      try {
    69→        switch (event.type) {
    70→          case "session.created": {
    71→            const session = (event as any).properties?.info
    72→            if (!session?.id) break
    73→            // Reset per-session tracking state when switching sessions.
    74→            if (currentSessionID !== session.id) {
    75→              seenUserMessages.clear()
    76→              messageStore.clear()
    77→              currentModel = null
    78→            }
    79→            currentSessionID = session.id
    80→            await callHook("session-start", {
    81→              session_id: session.id,
    82→            })
    83→            break
    84→          }
    85→
    86→          case "message.updated": {
    87→            const msg = (event as any).properties?.info
    88→            if (!msg) break
    89→            // Store message metadata (role, time, tokens, etc.)
    90→            messageStore.set(msg.id, msg)
    91→            // Track model from assistant messages
    92→            if (msg.role === "assistant" && msg.modelID) {
    93→              currentModel = msg.modelID
    94→            }
    95→            break
    96→          }
    97→
    98→          case "message.part.updated": {
    99→            const part = (event as any).properties?.part
   100→            if (!part?.messageID) break
   101→
   102→            // Fire turn-start on the first text part of a new user message
   103→            const msg = messageStore.get(part.messageID)
   104→            if (msg?.role === "user" && part.type === "text" && !seenUserMessages.has(msg.id)) {
   105→              seenUserMessages.add(msg.id)
   106→              const sessionID = msg.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
   107→              if (sessionID) {
   108→                await callHook("turn-start", {
   109→                  session_id: sessionID,
   110→                  prompt: part.text ?? "",
   111→                  model: currentModel ?? "",
   112→                })

Author: Daniel Adams <daniel@entire.io>
Date:   Wed Mar 25 14:03:08 2026 +0100

    fix(opencode): handle session.idle event for turn-end detection
    
    OpenCode stopped reliably emitting `session.status` events with
    `status.type === "idle"` after a recent update (~v1.3.x). Instead,
    it now emits `session.idle` events. The plugin only listened for
    `session.status`, causing turn-end hooks to never fire.
    
    Without turn-end, `PrepareTranscript` never runs, the transcript file
    is never created, and condensation silently fails on every commit with:
    "transcript not found at .entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json: file does not exist"
    
    This results in empty checkpoint directories on the metadata branch —
    the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is added to commits but no session data
    is written to `entire/checkpoints/v1`.
    
    Handle both `session.idle` and `session.status` (with idle type) as a
    fall-through case for cross-version compatibility.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

```typescript
case "session.idle":
case "session.status": {
  // session.status fires with status.type "idle" when the agent finishes.
  // session.idle is a separate event that some OpenCode versions emit instead.
  // Handle both for compatibility across OpenCode versions.
  let sessionID: string | null = null
  if (event.type === "session.idle") {
    sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
  } else {
    const props = (event as any).properties
    if (props?.status?.type !== "idle") break
    sessionID = props?.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
  }
  // ... rest of handler
}
```

# OpenCode Repository Analysis

## What is this repository?

This is the official OpenCode project—"The open source AI coding agent." It's a terminal-based AI assistant for software development maintained by the anomalyco organization.

## Is this the current/active project?

Yes, definitively. The repository shows:
- **130k stars** and **13.8k forks**, indicating substantial community adoption
- **740 releases** with the latest (v1.3.2) dated March 24, 2026
- **10,550 commits** on the dev branch
- **828 contributors** actively involved
- Recent activity across multiple installation methods and platforms

## Relationship to other projects

The search mentions "opencode-ai/opencode" and "sst/opencode," but this page (anomalyco/opencode) is the canonical source. The repository explicitly addresses this in its FAQ, clarifying that OpenCode is "100% open source" and "not coupled to any provider," distinguishing itself from Claude Code while remaining compatible with multiple AI models.

## Key distinguishing features

The project emphasizes its terminal-user-interface (TUI) focus, describing itself as built by "neovim users and the creators of terminal.shop," with aspirations to "push the limits of what's possible in the terminal."

# OpenCode Session.idle Event Feature Request Summary

## About session.idle

The `session.idle` event is triggered when an OpenCode session transitions to an idle state. Currently, plugin event handlers for this event are **fire-and-forget**, meaning the system doesn't wait for async operations to complete before moving on.

## Feature Request Details

**Issue #16879** proposes adding an `event.sync` hook to allow plugins to block the idle transition with awaitable operations.

### Current Problem

As described: "Plugin `event` handlers are fire-and-forget — the return promise is dropped"

This prevents plugins from performing critical tasks like commits, pushes, or CI polling that must complete before the session ends.

### Use Case

The requestor runs OpenCode as a coding agent in a sandbox environment. They need to report CI results back via `session.prompt()` before session completion, but currently results arrive as delayed follow-ups due to the non-blocking nature of event handlers.

### Proposed Solution

Add a synchronous `event.sync` hook that is awaited, while keeping the original `event` hook fire-and-forget for backwards compatibility. This allows selective blocking of the idle transition without breaking existing implementations.

## Related Issues

The request references #16626 (session.stopping hook) and #12472 (awaitable Stop hook mechanism) as related efforts with similar goals.

## Status

**Closed as duplicate of #16626** — same core need identified.

# Session Status Reporting Issues in OpenCode

## Core Problem

The `/session/status` endpoint fails to properly track asynchronous session states. When clients send commands via `/session/{session_id}/prompt_async`, the server loses visibility into the session's operational state.

## Status Reporting Issues

**Expected behavior:** Session status should transition through states (streaming → idle) and remain trackable via `/session/status`.

**Actual behavior:** Status remains "unknown" indefinitely. The documentation describes proper state transitions, but asynchronous operations bypass this tracking mechanism entirely.

## Events Involved

- `session.status_changed`: Server-Sent Events (SSE) that should emit when sessions transition states
- `session.idle`: Expected final state after async operations complete
- Status values should include: `streaming`, `idle`, `unknown`, and error states

## Technical Issues

The error message reveals a related problem: "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'agent.model')" at line 830 of `src/session/prompt.ts`. The `Agent.get()` call returns null when an invalid or missing agent is provided, causing downstream failures.

## Fixes Discussed

Pull request #12922 addresses these issues by:
- Setting session status to "busy" immediately when `prompt_async` is invoked
- Ensuring status resets to idle on failure
- Adding null-checking for the agent lookup to prevent TypeErrors

The fix prevents fire-and-forget prompts from leaving sessions permanently in unknown states.

# Session.idle Race Condition Analysis

## Core Issue

The problem occurs in non-interactive `opencode run` mode where a timing vulnerability allows continuation directives to be injected after `session.idle` fires while run teardown is already starting. This creates malformed assistant messages with empty payloads.

## What Happens During Teardown

According to the issue report, the sequence is:

1. `session.idle` event publishes (line 364 of trace log)
2. Run disposal begins almost simultaneously (line 365)
3. Continuation directive posts to `/session/.../message` endpoint (line 382)
4. Session disposal completes (line 503)

The reporter states: "continuation enqueue and run-mode disposal are not serialized, allowing continuation to be posted during teardown."

## Current session.idle Handling

The `session.idle` event currently triggers plugin hooks that inject ULW/Ralph continuation directives. However, there's no mechanism preventing this injection when run mode is ending. The reporter demonstrated that disabling these hooks at five specific locations in the plugin bundle prevents the issue locally, but this doesn't address the core sequencing problem.

## The Malformed State

Empty continuation assistant turns manifest as `"parts": []` in exported session JSON. These represent incomplete message objects where the directive was posted but the teardown process prevented proper response generation.

## Requested Resolution

The fix requires serializing teardown with post-idle operations and deferring disposal until any injected continuation reaches a terminal state.

# Session Completion Monitoring in OpenCode

## Problem Statement

Users report that the `session.idle` event fires before the agent has actually completed work, making it unreliable for deterministic session monitoring. The SDK doesn't guarantee when a session has truly finished.

## Available Approaches

### 1. **Database Query Method (Recommended Workaround)**

Query the local SQLite database at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` to check the last assistant message's finish status:

- Check `last_finish` field for value `"stop"` = session completed normally
- Value `"tool-calls"` = agent interrupted mid-operation
- Value `"content-filter"` = response blocked
- No completion timestamp = still in-progress

**Example:** "opencode status --session ses_xxx | get status" returns completed/idle/in-progress.

### 2. **Event Limitations**

The `session.idle` event alone is insufficient because:
- Background tasks like title generation continue after the event fires
- Message API can hang indefinitely if a session stalls
- Multiple idle events may fire without actual completion

### 3. **Outstanding Feature Gap**

No deterministic hook or API method currently exists in the SDK to reliably detect when an agent stops working and awaits user input. Related feature requests (#3169, #5515) acknowledge this limitation.

## Recommendation

Until native SDK support arrives, query the local database to inspect the last message's finish reason for authoritative completion status.

# Session Status Event Definitions

Based on the file content, here are the event definitions and emission logic:

## Event Definitions

The `SessionStatus.Event` object defines two events:

1. **Status Event** - `"session.status"`: Emitted with `sessionID` and `status` payload
2. **Idle Event** - `"session.idle"`: Deprecated event with just `sessionID` payload

## Emission Logic

Events fire in the `set` function (lines 89-100):

```typescript
yield* Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(Event.Status, { sessionID, status }))
if (status.type === "idle") {
  yield* Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(Event.Idle, { sessionID }))
  data.delete(sessionID)
  return
}
data.set(sessionID, status)
```

**When they fire:**
- `Status` event: Always published when status changes
- `Idle` event: Only when status type equals `"idle"` (then the entry is removed from the map)
- For non-idle statuses (`retry`, `busy`), the status persists in the map

The status can be one of three types: idle, retry (with attempt/message/next fields), or busy.

### 2. Relationship between `session.idle` and `session.status`

They are **two separate events that fire at the same time** when a session becomes idle:

- **`session.status`** is the primary event. It fires on every status change (busy, retry, idle). Its payload includes both `sessionID` and `status` (which is a union of `{ type: "idle" }`, `{ type: "busy" }`, or `{ type: "retry"; attempt; message; next }`).
- **`session.idle`** is a legacy/deprecated convenience event. It fires **only** when the status transitions to idle, with just `{ sessionID }` in its payload.

The emission logic in `status.ts` shows that `session.status` is always published on status change, and `session.idle` is additionally published only when `status.type === "idle"`. So `session.idle` is a subset signal of `session.status`.

### 3. Recent changes and known issues

**Repository context:** The original `opencode-ai/opencode` repo is **archived** (as of September 2025). The active project lives at `anomalyco/opencode` (130k+ stars, latest release v1.3.2 on March 24, 2026).

- **Issue #3815**: `session.idle` is not deterministic for session completion -- background tasks (title generation, etc.) can continue after it fires, and multiple idle events may fire without actual completion. === v1.3.2 (2026-03-24T22:50:58Z) ===
## TUI

- Added heap snapshot functionality allowing users to capture memory snapshots of both TUI and server processes via the "Write heap snapshot" command. Snapshots are saved to `tui.heapsnapshot` and `server.heapsnapshot` files.


=== v1.3.1 (2026-03-24T22:07:48Z) ===
## Features

- Added Poe as a built-in authentication provider with OAuth and API key support (#18477)
- Enabled token caching for custom Amazon Bedrock providers (#18959)
- Added syntax highlighting support for Kotlin, HCL, Lua, and TOML files (#18198)
- Added manual lock/unlock for theme mode (#18905)

## Fixes

- Fixed session timeline jumping when scrolling (#18993)
- Fixed GitLab Duo Workflow models showing incorrect identity (#18928)
- Fixed theme mode switching between dark and light modes (#18851)
- Fixed console account URL handling for better navigation (#18809)
- Fixed session busy state handling for better responsiveness (#18758)
- Fixed stale session hover preview (#18727)
- Fixed project hover state (#18732)
- Fixed prompt history navigation (#18775)
- Fixed filtering of non-renderable part types (#18926)
- Fixed ProviderIcon optional chaining issue (#18927)
- Fixed process cleanup when closing terminal tabs (#16057)
- Fixed batching of multi-file prompt attachments via picker, paste, and drag-drop (#18722)
- Fixed patch tool counts visibility when displaying files with long names (#18678)
- Fixed project avatar popover flicker when switching projects via sidebar (#18660)

## Improvements

- Improved startup efficiency (#18985)
- Updated Feishu community links for Chinese (zh) locales (#18975)
- Improved file tree panel to maintain its minimum width when resized (#18777)
- Improved desktop app stability with more robust sidecar process cleanup (#18742)
- Changed command palette shortcut to `Cmd+K` (with `Cmd+P` still working as fallback) (#18731)
- Restored keyboard project switching in open sidebar with proper Enter key activation (#18682)

=== v1.3.0 (2026-03-22T23:32:25Z) ===
## Important

- Removed anthropic oauth plugin, see: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/18186/changes

## New Features

- **GitLab Agent Platform** (#18014): GitLab Agent Platform is now fully supported with automatic discovery of workflow models from your GitLab instance. Workflow models can use opencode's local tools (file read/write, shell, etc.) over WebSocket.
- **Git-backed Session Review** (#17961): Added git-backed session review modes, enabling users to review uncommitted changes and branch diffs directly within opencode. Git changes are now the default review source with the desktop review tree staying synchronized with your selected source.
- **Multistep Authentication** (#18103, #18035): TUI and Desktop both support multistep authentication flows which means providers like Github Copilot for Enterprise deployments now work as intended
- **Interactive Update Flow** (#18662): Major and minor updates now show a confirmation dialog before upgrading, allowing you to review changes before updating. You can also skip specific versions if you prefer to stay on your current release.
- **Node.js Support** (#18324): opencode can now run on Node.js in addition to Bun, with a dedicated Node.js entry point and build script that bundles the server with database migrations.

## Desktop App Improvements

- **Project Navigation** (#18502): Navigate between projects faster using keyboard shortcuts (cmd+option+arrow keys).
- **File Uploads** (#18403): Desktop app now supports file type filters and multiple file selection when uploading files.
- **Workspace Switching** (#18207): Fixed visual flickering when switching between workspaces or projects - the interface now transitions smoothly without showing loading spinners during navigation.
- **Sidebar Resize** (#18647): Fixed issue where sidebar would automatically close when being resized to minimum width. The sidebar now clamps at minimum width instead of closing.
- **Loading States** (#18501): Improved loading state management across the app for smoother, more consistent feedback during async operations.
- **Console Login** (#18281): Fixed console device login to properly handle pending authorization states, ensuring the login process continues polling instead of failing while waiting for approval.

## Terminal & Editor

- **Terminal Rename** (#18263): Fixed terminal renaming from the context menu, which previously failed due to dropdown focus conflicts.
- **Terminal Error Recovery** (#17591): Fixed an issue where terminals would become unresponsive when the server returned a "not found" error for terminal sessions. Terminals now properly reinitialize and remain interactive.
- **Paste Operations** (#18079): Paste operations now preserve raw byte data, enabling proper handling of binary content and special characters when pasting into the terminal.
- **Prevent Duplicate Submits** (#18148): Fixed issue where rapidly pressing Enter could submit prompts multiple times. Now ignores repeated Enter submits.

## Providers & Models

- **xAI Responses API** (#18175): Improved xAI reasoning models performance in long multi-turn conversations by switching to the responses API with encrypted content support.
- **GPT Model List** (#18101): Updated the GPT subscription model list with the latest available models.
- **Vertex AI Fix** (#18283): Fixed Vertex AI errors with non-thinking models (like gemini-2.0-flash) by only applying thinking configuration to models that support reasoning capabilities.
- **vLLM Context Overflow** (#17763): Improved error detection for vLLM context overflow errors, providing clearer feedback when context limits are exceeded during inference.
- **Cost Chunk Format** (#16817): Fixed streaming error where cost data was sent in upstream provider format instead of client-requested format, preventing validation errors when mixing provider formats.

## Review & Collaboration

- **File Attachments** (#17815): Fixed file and image attachments being silently lost when reusing or forking a previous prompt with attachments.
- **Snapshot Revert** (#18093): Fixed snapshot revert issues where overlapping file changes could apply the wrong patch hash, and resolved a sorting bug in hidden file ordering.

## Authentication & Account

- **Stale Credentials** (#18426): Fixed stale server URL and email on re-login. Previously, logging into a different server could fail due to cached credentials from a previous environment.
- **Codex Access** (#18337): OAuth plan users can now access codex instructions freely without the previous whitelisting restrictions.

## UI/UX Improvements

- **Theme Improvements** (#17958): Improved UI contrast and reduced brightness of hover/active elements for better readability and reduced eye strain.
- **System Prompt** (#18140): Cleaner AI responses with a streamlined fallback system prompt that removes unnecessary boilerplate text.
- **Agent & Skill Ordering** (#18261): More consistent AI responses with improved prompt caching by stabilizing the order of agents and skills in system prompts.

## Bug Fixes

- **Remote Server Switching** (#17214): Fixed issues when switching between remote servers that caused stale project data, broken terminal spawning, and sidebar showing incorrect projects.
- **Windows Commands** (#18010): Fixed Windows command execution for shims (.cmd/.bat files) to resolve failures during upgrades, uninstalls, IDE installs, and LSP launches.
- **Tool Discovery** (#18320): Fixed tool discovery for npm-installed packages by including the cache bin directory in PATH lookups, ensuring locally installed tools are properly found.
- **Error Messages** (#18165): Tool and session error messages now display in clean, human-readable format instead of showing confusing technical error strings.
- **Chunk Timeout** (#18264): Disabled chunk timeout by default to prevent issues across various use cases; users can still enable it in their configuration if needed.
- **Event Ordering** (#18259): Events in real-time streams now process sequentially in order, ensuring consistent and predictable event display instead of potentially out-of-order delivery.
- **Desktop Stability** (#18300): Improved desktop stability with more reliable workspace and session routing, fixing sidebar selection mismatches and race conditions when switching projects.

**Thank you to 16 community contributors:**
- @jquense:
  - fix(opencode): preserve prompt tool enables with empty agent permissions (#17064)
- @bugulo:
  - fix(app): agent switch should not reset thinking level (#17470)
- @ghost91-:
  - fix(core): consider code: context_length_exceeded as context overflow in API call errors (#17748)
  - fix(core): detect vLLM context overflow errors (#17763)
- @Tarquinen:
  - fix(opencode): apply message transforms during compaction (#17823)
- @AbigailJixiangyuyu:
  - fix(windows): restore /editor support on Windows (#17146)
- @altendky:
  - fix(tui): check for selected text instead of any selection in dialog escape handler (#16779)
  - docs: add describe annotation to snapshot config field (#17861)
- @OpeOginni:
  - docs: mark tools config as deprecated (#17951)
  - docs(cli): update experimental TY LSP flag description for clarity across multiple languages (#14770)
  - fix(desktop): fix error handling by adding errorName function to identify NotFoundError rather than statusCode (#17591)
  - fix(desktop): remote server switching (#17214)
- @ariane-emory:
  - fix: Add apply_patch to EDIT_TOOLS filter (#18009)
- @anduimagui:
  - fix(app): ignore repeated Enter submits in prompt input (#18148)
- @jorgitin02:
  - fix: stabilize agent and skill ordering in prompt descriptions (#18261)
- @Jaaneek:
  - feat: switch xai provider to responses API (#18175)
- @mchenco:
  - docs: add Cloudflare Workers AI provider (#18322)
- @vglafirov:
  - feat: enable GitLab Agent Platform with workflow model discovery (#18014)
- @github-actions[bot]:

This is the commit *just before* the deprecation (`8b19c6c7e4` - "better retry display"). At this point, `session.status` with `type: "idle"` was already being emitted -- there was no separate `session.idle` event yet.

Here is the complete analysis:

---

## Findings: OpenCode Session Status / Session Idle Event History

### The Claim is INCORRECT

The claim that "OpenCode 1.3.x changed session.status so that it no longer emits status.type 'idle'" is **false**. The actual situation is the opposite:

### What Actually Happened (Chronological)

**1. Original behavior (before v1.0.69)**
- `session.status` was the ONLY event for status changes
- It emitted all three types: `"idle"`, `"busy"`, `"retry"`
- There was a separate `SessionPrompt.Event.Idle` (`"session.idle"`) defined in `prompt.ts`, but it was **never published** (dead code)
- File: `packages/opencode/src/session/status.ts` at commit `8b19c6c7e4`

**2. Commit `bdfa213ccf` (2025-11-17) -- "deprecated session.idle event"**
- Despite the misleading commit message, this commit actually **added** the `session.idle` event as a **backward-compatibility shim**
- Moved the `session.idle` event definition from `prompt.ts` into `status.ts`
- Added logic so that when `SessionStatus.set()` is called with `type: "idle"`, it **also** publishes a `session.idle` event
- The event definition is marked with `// deprecated` in the code
- First included in **v1.0.69** (released 2025-11-17)

**3. Current behavior (v1.3.2, dev branch)**
Both events fire simultaneously. In `status.ts`, the `set()` function does:
```typescript
if (status.type === "idle") {
  yield* Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(Event.Idle, { sessionID }))
  data.delete(sessionID)
  return
}
```
So when the agent finishes a turn:
1. `session.status` fires with `{ status: { type: "idle" } }` -- **always**
2. `session.idle` fires with `{ sessionID }` -- **also always** (as a deprecated compat event)

### Key Details

- **`"idle"` is still a valid status.type** -- the Zod schema union in `SessionStatus.Info` still includes `z.literal("idle")`. This is confirmed in both the source code and the generated SDK types (`EventSessionStatus`, `SessionStatus` types in `types.gen.ts`).

- **Both events fire on every idle transition** -- `session.status` with `type: "idle"` AND `session.idle` are published together. The `session.idle` event is a redundant/deprecated convenience.

- **The SSE event stream forwards ALL bus events** -- `server/routes/event.ts` uses `Bus.subscribeAll()` to forward every event to connected clients, so both events are visible over SSE.

- **The SDK types include both** -- `types.gen.ts` defines both `EventSessionStatus` and `EventSessionIdle` in the event union type.

### Your CLI's Plugin Already Handles This Correctly

The plugin at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin.ts` (lines 118-139) correctly handles both events:
```typescript
case "session.idle":
case "session.status": {
  // session.status fires with status.type "idle" when the agent finishes.
  // session.idle is a separate event that some OpenCode versions emit instead.
  // Handle both for compatibility across OpenCode versions.
```

However, the comment "some OpenCode versions emit instead" is slightly inaccurate -- no version emits `session.idle` *instead of* `session.status`. The history is:
- Before v1.0.69: Only `session.status` with `type: "idle"` (no `session.idle`)
- v1.0.69 onward: Both `session.status` with `type: "idle"` AND `session.idle` (deprecated compat)

### Relevant Commits
| Commit | Date | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `a1214fff2e` | 2025-11-17 | Refactor agent loop (#4412) -- `session.idle` defined in prompt.ts but never published |
| `8b19c6c7e4` | 2025-11-17 | "better retry display" -- only `session.status` with idle/busy/retry |
| `bdfa213ccf` | 2025-11-17 | "deprecated session.idle event" -- **added** `session.idle` as compat shim alongside `session.status` idle |
| `10a3d6c54e` | 2025-03-21 | "effectify SessionStatus service (#18565)" -- refactored to Effect, kept both events |

### Version Timeline
- **v1.0.68 and earlier**: Only `session.status` with `type: "idle"` fires
- **v1.0.69 through v1.3.2 (current)**: Both `session.status` with `type: "idle"` AND `session.idle` fire

Here are the complete findings from all the fetched files:

---

## 1. `status.ts` (dev branch and v1.3.2 tag -- identical content; main branch returned 404)

**The critical `set()` function:**

```typescript
const set = Effect.fn("SessionStatus.set")(function* (sessionID: SessionID, status: Info) {
  const data = yield* InstanceState.get(state)
  yield* Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(Event.Status, { sessionID, status }))
  if (status.type === "idle") {
    yield* Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(Event.Idle, { sessionID }))
    data.delete(sessionID)
    return
  }
  data.set(sessionID, status)
})
```

**Answer to your question: BOTH events are published when the status is "idle".**

The execution order is:
1. `Bus.publish(Event.Status, { sessionID, status })` is called **unconditionally** first -- this publishes `session.status` with `{ sessionID, status: { type: "idle" } }`
2. Then, **if** `status.type === "idle"`, it **also** publishes `Bus.publish(Event.Idle, { sessionID })` -- this is the `session.idle` event
3. After that, it deletes the session from the in-memory map and returns

So `session.idle` is a **deprecated convenience duplicate** of the idle case. The comment `// deprecated` on the `Idle` event definition confirms this. When a session becomes idle, an SSE client will receive **two** events in sequence:
- `session.status` with `properties: { sessionID, status: { type: "idle" } }`
- `session.idle` with `properties: { sessionID }`

## 2. `event.ts` (SSE route)

The SSE route uses `Bus.subscribeAll()` which subscribes to the wildcard `"*"` key. The `Bus.publish()` function iterates over both the specific event type subscribers AND the `"*"` subscribers, calling each one. So **every** bus event (including both `session.status` and `session.idle`) gets forwarded to connected SSE clients.

## 3. `bus/index.ts` (Bus implementation)

content.text:
Here are the complete findings from all the fetched files:

---

## 1. `status.ts` (dev branch and v1.3.2 tag -- identical content; main branch returned 404)

**The critical `set()` function:**

```typescript
const set = Effect.fn("SessionStatus.set")(function* (sessionID: SessionID, status: Info) {
  const data = yield* InstanceState.get(state)
  yield* Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(Event.Status, { sessionID, status }))
  if (status.type === "idle") {
    yield* Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(Event.Idle, { sessionID }))
    data.delete(sessionID)
    return
  }
  data.set(sessionID, status)
})
```

**Answer to your question: BOTH events are published when the status is "idle".**

The execution order is:
1. `Bus.publish(Event.Status, { sessionID, status })` is called **unconditionally** first -- this publishes `session.status` with `{ sessionID, status: { type: "idle" } }`
2. Then, **if** `status.type === "idle"`, it **also** publishes `Bus.publish(Event.Idle, { sessionID })` -- this is the `session.idle` event
3. After that, it deletes the session from the in-memory map and returns

So `session.idle` is a **deprecated convenience duplicate** of the idle case. The comment `// deprecated` on the `Idle` event definition confirms this. When a session becomes idle, an SSE client will receive **two** events in sequence:
- `session.status` with `properties: { sessionID, status: { type: "idle" } }`
- `session.idle` with `properties: { sessionID }`

## 2. `event.ts` (SSE route)

The SSE route uses `Bus.subscribeAll()` which subscribes to the wildcard `"*"` key. The `Bus.publish()` function iterates over both the specific event type subscribers AND the `"*"` subscribers, calling each one. So **every** bus event (including both `session.status` and `session.idle`) gets forwarded to connected SSE clients.

## 3. `bus/index.ts` (Bus implementation)

The `publish()` function:
```typescript
for (const key of [def.type, "*"]) {
  const match = [...(state().subscriptions.get(key) ?? [])]
  for (const sub of match) {
    pending.push(sub(payload))
  }
}
```
This confirms that both specific-type subscribers and wildcard (`"*"`) subscribers receive every published event. There is no filtering or suppression.

## Summary

Your CLI's fix to handle `session.idle` is correct for turn-end detection. However, you could alternatively (or additionally) listen for `session.status` events where `status.type === "idle"` -- both events are always emitted when the agent finishes. The `session.idle` event is marked as deprecated, which suggests that upstream may eventually remove it in favor of clients just checking `session.status` with `type: "idle"`.

Here's the contradiction: **the OpenCode source code clearly publishes both events** — `session.status` with `type: "idle"` fires first, then `session.idle` fires second. There's no version where one is skipped.

But your colleague's local debugging says they only see `status.type === "busy"`, never `"idle"`. So the question is: **what's happening between the Bus publish and the plugin receiving the event?**

A few hypotheses worth investigating:

1. **Plugin event handler is fire-and-forget on `session.idle`** — OpenCode issue #16879 documents that plugin event handlers for `session.idle` have their promise dropped. In `opencode run` mode, the process may start tearing down after `session.idle` fires, and the `session.status` idle event might arrive *after* the plugin's event loop is already dead. The plugin would see all the `busy` status events during the turn, but the final `idle` status event gets lost in shutdown.

2. **Event ordering in the SSE stream** — the `set()` function does `yield* Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(...))` which wraps in an Effect. If the Effect runtime processes these asynchronously, there could be a race where `session.idle` gets delivered but `session.status` idle doesn't complete before teardown.

3. **The plugin might be getting called but the `break` short-circuits** — if somehow two `session.status` events arrive (one `busy`, one `idle`) and the plugin processes the `busy` one and breaks before seeing the `idle` one.

Want me to:
- **A)** Add some debug logging to the plugin to trace exactly which events arrive and in what order (to confirm what your colleague saw)?
- **B)** Just accept the fix as-is — handling both `session.idle` and `session.status` is the right defensive approach regardless of root cause?
- **C)** Dig into the OpenCode plugin loading mechanism to understand how events are dispatched to plugins (vs SSE clients)?

content.text:
No — `busy` isn't new and its meaning hasn't changed. The `Info` type has had all three values since `status.ts` was first created in v1.0.69:

- `"busy"` — agent is actively working (turn in progress)
- `"idle"` — agent finished (turn ended)
- `"retry"` — hit a retryable error, waiting

The schema is **identical** between v1.0.69 and v1.3.2. `busy` has always meant "working", not "done."

So your colleague's observation is the interesting part: they see `session.status` events with `type: "busy"` arriving at the plugin, but the `type: "idle"` one never arrives — even though the source code publishes it. Meanwhile `session.idle` (the separate event) does arrive.

This points to a runtime issue rather than a semantic change — likely the Effect-TS refactor in v1.3.x introduced a race where `opencode run` tears down after processing `session.idle` but before the `session.status` idle event reaches the plugin. The `set()` function publishes `session.status` first, but both go through `Effect.promise(() => Bus.publish(...))`, and the plugin dispatch might be async enough that the process exits between the two.

**Bottom line:** The fix on this branch is correct — `session.idle` is the reliable turn-end signal in practice. But the PR description and comments should probably be updated to reflect that this is likely a race condition in event delivery, not a deliberate API change by OpenCode.

No deduplication — `handleLifecycleTurnEnd` will run every time it's called. So yes, if both `session.idle` and `session.status` with `type: "idle"` fire (which the source says they do), the plugin calls `turn-end` twice, and the CLI processes the checkpoint twice.

The fix as written is **buggy for versions where both events fire**. It would double-fire `turn-end` on v1.0.69 through v1.3.2.

The correct approach is one of:
1. **Only listen for `session.idle`** — it fires on all versions since v1.0.69, and it's the one that empirically works. Drop the `session.status` idle check entirely.
2. **Deduplicate in the plugin** — e.g., track a `lastTurnEndSessionID` and skip if already fired for this turn.
3. **Only listen for `session.status`** and figure out why the idle status isn't reaching the plugin.

Option 1 seems simplest — do you want me to update the plugin to drop the `session.status` idle path and rely solely on `session.idle`?

import { Installation } from "@/installation"
import { Provider } from "@/provider/provider"
import { Log } from "@/util/log"
import {
  streamText,
  wrapLanguageModel,
  type ModelMessage,
  type StreamTextResult,
  type Tool,
  type ToolSet,
  tool,
  jsonSchema,
} from "ai"
import { mergeDeep, pipe } from "remeda"
import { GitLabWorkflowLanguageModel } from "gitlab-ai-provider"
import { ProviderTransform } from "@/provider/transform"
import { Config } from "@/config/config"
import { Instance } from "@/project/instance"
import type { Agent } from "@/agent/agent"
import type { MessageV2 } from "./message-v2"
import { Plugin } from "@/plugin"
import { SystemPrompt } from "./system"
import { Flag } from "@/flag/flag"
import { Permission } from "@/permission"
import { Auth } from "@/auth"

export namespace LLM {
  const log = Log.create({ service: "llm" })
  export const OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX = ProviderTransform.OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX

  export type StreamInput = {
    user: MessageV2.User
    sessionID: string
    model: Provider.Model
    agent: Agent.Info
    permission?: Permission.Ruleset
    system: string[]
    abort: AbortSignal
    messages: ModelMessage[]
    small?: boolean
    tools: Record<string, Tool>
    retries?: number
    toolChoice?: "auto" | "required" | "none"
  }

  export type StreamOutput = StreamTextResult<ToolSet, unknown>

  export async function stream(input: StreamInput) {
    const l = log
      .clone()
      .tag("providerID", input.model.providerID)
      .tag("modelID", input.model.id)
      .tag("sessionID", input.sessionID)
      .tag("small", (input.small ?? false).toString())
      .tag("agent", input.agent.name)
      .tag("mode", input.agent.mode)
    l.info("stream", {
      modelID: input.model.id,
      providerID: input.model.providerID,
    })
    const [language, cfg, provider, auth] = await Promise.all([
      Provider.getLanguage(input.model),
      Config.get(),
      Provider.getProvider(input.model.providerID),
      Auth.get(input.model.providerID),
    ])
    // TODO: move this to a proper hook
    const isOpenaiOauth = provider.id === "openai" && auth?.type === "oauth"

    const system: string[] = []
    system.push(
      [
        // use agent prompt otherwise provider prompt
        ...(input.agent.prompt ? [input.agent.prompt] : SystemPrompt.provider(input.model)),
        // any custom prompt passed into this call
